title: Compact-support finiteness and Frobenius
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum
$p,a,q,k_0,k$, where $q=p^a$, choose a prime $\ell\neq p$, write
$\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, choose an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$, and
choose a finite extension $E/\Ql$ contained in $\Qlb$. Let $Y_0$ be a
separated finite-type
$k_0$-scheme, put $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$, and choose
$K\in D^b_{c,\mathrm W}(Y,E)$, a
Weil complex. Write $E_Y$ for the constant
Weil sheaf. Then the
$E$-coefficient abbreviations mean
$H^i(Y,E)=H^i(Y,E_Y)$ and $H_c^i(Y,E)=H_c^i(Y,E_Y)$. The
ordinary and compact-support
cohomology groups, in particular $H_c^i(Y,K)$ meaning
$H_c^i(Y,\operatorname{For}K)$, are finite-dimensional, vanish outside a
finite interval, and carry the
geometric Frobenius
automorphism. If $Y_0$ is
proper, the
canonical isomorphism

$$
H_c^i(Y,K)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^i(Y,K)
$$

is Frobenius-equivariant.
If $Y$ has dimension $e\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$ and $K=E_Y$ is the
constant Weil sheaf, then

$$
H_c^i(Y,E)=0\qquad\text{for }i<0\text{ or }i>2e.
$$

For proper $Y$, the
ordinary cohomology also
satisfies $H^i(Y,E)=0$ for $i<0$ or $i>2e$. In
particular, if $X_0/\Fq$ is smooth,
proper, geometrically connected of pure dimension
$d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, and $X=X_0\times_{\Fq}k$, then

$$
H^i(X,\Ql)=0\qquad\text{for }i\notin[0,2d].
$$

Moreover, if $Y_0$ is geometrically connected (neither properness nor
smoothness is needed), then $H^0(Y,E)\cong E$, and the
geometric Frobenius acts as the
identity on this group; in particular $H^0(X,\Ql)\cong\Ql$ with
$F=\mathrm{id}$ for every smooth, separated finite-type, geometrically
connected $X_0$.

proof.text: *Step 1 (the setting).* $Y_0\to\Spec k_0$ is separated and of finite type, so by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change] its base change $a_Y:Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k\to s=\Spec k$ is separated and of finite type [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]; this is the setting of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport] and [def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius]. For a Weil complex $K=(\operatorname{For}K,\theta_K)\in D^b_{c,\mathrm W}(Y,E)$ [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], $\operatorname{For}K\in D^b_c(Y,E)$ and $\theta_K:Lg_Y^*\operatorname{For}K\to\operatorname{For}K$ is an isomorphism, and $H^i(Y,K)$, $H^i_c(Y,K)$ mean $H^i(Y,\operatorname{For}K)$, $H^i_c(Y,\operatorname{For}K)$ [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology]. The constant Weil sheaf is $(E_Y,\theta_E)$ with its canonical Weil structure [def-weil-constant-weil-structure], and $\operatorname{For}(E_Y,\theta_E)=E_Y$, so $H^i(Y,E)=H^i(Y,E_Y)$ and $H^i_c(Y,E)=H^i_c(Y,E_Y)$ are the case $K=E_Y$ of what follows.

source.place: ## Proof, Step 1 (setting: a_Y separated of finite type over k); Deligne, Weil I, (1.3)-(1.4), p. 274 (X_0 a variety over F_q and X its extension of scalars)

proof.text: *Step 2 (finite-dimensionality and boundedness).* Let $M=\operatorname{For}K\in D^b_c(Y,E)$. By [lem-weil-structure-direct-images-constructible] (with $\Lambda=E$), $Ra_{Y*}M$ and $Ra_{Y!}M$ lie in $D^b_c(s,E)$, the domain of the point fibre functor $\operatorname{Fib}_s:D^b_c(s,E)\to D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(E)$ of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] (item 3). Hence $\RGamma(Y,M)=\operatorname{Fib}_s(Ra_{Y*}M)$ and $\RGammac(Y,M)=\operatorname{Fib}_s(Ra_{Y!}M)$ [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] are objects of $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(E)$, which by [def-weil-point-fd-complexes] means: every $H^i(Y,M)=\mathrm H^i(\RGamma(Y,M))$ and every $H^i_c(Y,M)$ is a finite-dimensional $E$-vector space [def-weil-vector-space-dimension], and only finitely many of them are nonzero, so they vanish outside the finite interval $[i_-,i_+]$ spanned by the finitely many degrees in which they are nonzero (any interval if there are none). This is the asserted finite-dimensionality and vanishing outside a finite interval, for ordinary and for compact-support cohomology.

source.place: (1.3), p. 274 and (1.10), p. 277 (the H^i(X,F), H^i_c(X,F) are finite-dimensional Q_l-spaces, zero for i > 2 dim X); finite level: Milne, LEC (literature/milne-lectures-on-etale-cohomology_LEC.pdf), Theorem 19.1, p. 123, Proposition 18.3 (c), p. 120, and the l-adic groups p. 124; the reduction to constructibility at the point follows the blueprint ## Proof, Steps 2-4

proof.text: *Step 3 (the geometric Frobenius is an automorphism).* By [def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius] the geometric Frobenius on $H^i(Y,K)$ is $F=\mathrm H^i(\RGamma(Y,\theta_K))\circ\mathrm H^i(\tau_M)$ and on $H^i_c(Y,K)$ it is $F=\mathrm H^i(\RGammac(Y,\theta_K))\circ\mathrm H^i(\tau_{c,M})$, with $M=\operatorname{For}K$ and $\tau_M$, $\tau_{c,M}$ the transports of [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport]. The maps $\mathrm H^i(\tau_M)$, $\mathrm H^i(\tau_{c,M})$ are isomorphisms by [lem-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport-iso] (3); $\theta_K$ is an isomorphism (Step 1), so its images under the functors $\RGamma(Y,-)$, $\RGammac(Y,-)$ and $\mathrm H^i$ are isomorphisms. Each factor is $E$-linear, being $\mathrm H^i$ of a morphism of $D(E)$. So $F$ is an $E$-linear automorphism of the finite-dimensional space $H^i(Y,K)$, resp. $H^i_c(Y,K)$ (Step 2): these groups carry the geometric Frobenius automorphism.

source.place: (1.1.14), p. 153 (F acts on H^i(X,F) and H^i_c 'par transport de structure'); Deligne, Weil I, (1.12), p. 278 (F^*: H^i_c(X,F) -> H^i_c(X,F^*F) -> H^i_c(X,F))

proof.text:
*Step 4 (the proper case: the comparison is Frobenius-equivariant).* Let $Y_0$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Then $a_Y$ is proper, as a base change of $Y_0\to\Spec k_0$ [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change], and [prop-weil-proper-compact-coincidence] gives the natural isomorphism $\kappa_N:Ra_{Y!}N\xrightarrow{\sim}Ra_{Y*}N$ for $N\in D^b_c(Y,E)$, hence the canonical isomorphism $h=\mathrm H^i(\operatorname{Fib}_s\kappa_M):H^i_c(Y,K)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^i(Y,K)$, $M=\operatorname{For}K$. With $F_c$, $F$ the operators of Step 3:
$$F\circ h=\mathrm H^i(\RGamma(Y,\theta_K))\circ\mathrm H^i(\tau_M)\circ\mathrm H^i(\operatorname{Fib}_s\kappa_M)
=\mathrm H^i(\RGamma(Y,\theta_K))\circ\mathrm H^i(\operatorname{Fib}_s\kappa_{Lg_Y^*M})\circ\mathrm H^i(\tau_{c,M})$$
by [lem-pod-proper-coincidence-frobenius] (2), and $\RGamma(Y,\theta_K)\circ\operatorname{Fib}_s(\kappa_{Lg_Y^*M})=\operatorname{Fib}_s(Ra_{Y*}\theta_K\circ\kappa_{Lg_Y^*M})=\operatorname{Fib}_s(\kappa_M\circ Ra_{Y!}\theta_K)=\operatorname{Fib}_s(\kappa_M)\circ\RGammac(Y,\theta_K)$ by naturality of $\kappa$ applied to $\theta_K:Lg_Y^*M\to M$. Hence $F\circ h=h\circ\mathrm H^i(\RGammac(Y,\theta_K))\circ\mathrm H^i(\tau_{c,M})=h\circ F_c$: the canonical isomorphism $H^i_c(Y,K)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^i(Y,K)$ is Frobenius-equivariant.

source.place: ## Proof, Step 6; Deligne, Weil I (literature/deligne-weil-I_PMIHES-1974-43.pdf), (1.3), p. 274: 'Pour X propre, les deux coincident'

proof.text: Step 5 (ordinary constant-adic upper bound). For any finite-type scheme T over k0 of geometric dimension at most d, apply lem-sf-etale-direct-image-vanishing to its geometric structure map. The etale/pro-etale derived direct-image comparison transfers this bound to pro-etale sheaves of etale origin, for every finite coefficient ring. Apply lem-pod-adic-unit-direct-image-finite-bound with b=2d. Forgetting the Weil action commutes with ordinary derived direct image by prop-weil-operations, so the constant Weil complex, and any complex whose forgotten object is that constant unit in degree zero, has ordinary cohomology zero above 2d. All identifications are functorial isomorphisms; no arbitrary lattice is selected.

source.place: Theorems 15.1 and 19.2; §8.15 and Proposition 18.3(a), with §18 for compactification and proper coincidence

proof.text: Step 6 (a proper compactification and its boundary). Choose a dense proper compactification j:X -> Y with dim Y=dim X, using exists_dense_compactification from the proved dense-open dimension comparison. Let Z be its reduced closed complement. Field extension preserves dimension. Hence dim Y <= e. If the geometric fiber of Z is nonempty, Z and Y are nonempty, and the proved theorem topologicalKrullDim_compl_lt_of_dense gives dim Z < dim Y <= e. Since Z is finite type and nonempty its dimension is some natural number z<e. By Step 5 and proper compact-support coincidence, H_c^r(Y)=0 and H_c^(r-1)(Z)=0 for r>2e, since r-1>2z. If the geometric fiber of Z is empty its adic sheaf category is zero, so its compact-support cohomology vanishes in every degree. Pullback of the constant Weil object along j and Z -> Y is constant.

source.place: Theorems 15.1 and 19.2; §8.15 and Proposition 18.3(a), with §18 for compactification and proper coincidence

proof.text: Step 7 (compact-support vanishing by localization). Apply Ra_Y! to the open-closed triangle for the constant Weil complex on Y. The long exact cohomology sequence has H_c^(r-1)(Z) -> H_c^r(X) -> H_c^r(Y). Both outer groups vanish by Step 6, so the second map is injective into zero and H_c^r(X)=0. For r<0 use exact extension by zero followed by a right derived ordinary direct image of an object in degree zero; its negative homology is zero. This proves the unchanged constant compact-support range. The stronger comparison embedding lem-pod-compact-support-finite-coefficient-comparison is unused and withdrawn. The unit perfectness claims remain untouched.

source.place: Theorems 15.1 and 19.2; §8.15 and Proposition 18.3(a), with §18 for compactification and proper coincidence

proof.text: *Step 8 (ordinary cohomology of proper $Y$, and the case of $X$).* If $Y$ is proper, [prop-weil-proper-compact-coincidence] gives $H^i(Y,E)\cong H^i_c(Y,E)$, so $H^i(Y,E)=0$ for $i<0$ or $i>2e$ by Step 7. Now let $X_0$ be smooth, proper, geometrically connected of pure dimension $d$ [def-weil-geometric-hypotheses], $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, and $E=\Ql$. By [def-weil-geometric-hypotheses] every irreducible component of $X$ has Krull dimension $d$ [def-weil-pure-dimension]; a chain of nonempty irreducible closed subsets of $X$ lies in an irreducible component (its largest member is irreducible, hence contained in a maximal irreducible closed subset), so $\dim X\leq d$ [def-kun-dimension]. $X$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]. The case $Y=X$, $e=d$, $E=\Ql$ of the first sentence gives $H^i(X,\Ql)=0$ for $i\notin[0,2d]$.

source.place: (1.3), p. 274 ('Pour X propre, les deux coincident ... nuls pour i > 2 dim(X)'); Milne, LEC, Theorem 15.1, p. 105

proof.text: *Step 9 (degree zero for geometrically connected $Y_0$).* If $Y_0$ is geometrically connected [def-weil-geometric-hypotheses], then $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$ is nonempty and connected by [lem-weil-geometrically-connected-algebraic-closure] ($k$ is an algebraic closure of $k_0$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]); no properness or smoothness is used. By [lem-pod-connected-constant-h0] (3), $E\to H^0(Y,E)$, $\lambda\mapsto\lambda\cdot1_E$, is an isomorphism, so $H^0(Y,E)\cong E$. By [lem-pod-frobenius-fixes-unit-section], the geometric Frobenius $F$ of the constant Weil sheaf satisfies $F(1_E)=1_E$; $F$ is $E$-linear (Step 3), so $F(\lambda\cdot1_E)=\lambda\cdot1_E$ for all $\lambda\in E$, i.e. $F=\operatorname{id}$ on $H^0(Y,E)$. For a smooth, separated finite-type, geometrically connected $X_0$ and $E=\Ql$ this is $H^0(X,\Ql)\cong\Ql$ with $F=\operatorname{id}$.

source.place: (1.11)-(1.12), pp. 277-278 (F^* on a sheaf coming from X_0, identity on the constant sheaf's sections); the blueprint ## Proof, Step 7

proof_origin.place: Theorems 15.1 and 19.2; §8.15 and Proposition 18.3(a); Y5 uses the existing ordinary finite-coefficient bound, dense compactification and localization. Steps 5-7 follow the Lean proof in Finiteness; other clauses are retained.
